evidence_status: No consciousness-indicator experiment has been run
experimental_world: Latent Worlds ecology (apparatus, not target claim)
primary_question: Can an agent evolve and causally use information about its own computation, beyond an external world model?

indicators.name: Causal self-model and self/world discrimination
indicators.primary_test: novel internal-competence lesions versus externally generated matched error, with causal adaptation outcome
controls: self-state shuffled with another agent at the same time
indicators.required_evidence: benefit on external reward under equal baseline performance, lost after selective self-state lesion and replicated across new world laws

indicators.name: Selective global availability
indicators.primary_test: flexible use of selected internal information by multiple task-specialist processes after held-out task changes
indicators.required_evidence: selective causal global access with same compute and input budget, replicated on new tasks/worlds

indicators.name: Recursive internal reliability regulation
indicators.primary_test: agent internally predicts changes in precision of its own inference under held-out perturbations and changes action
indicators.required_evidence: novel-perturbation action benefit conditional on standard confidence, selective lesion effect, separate from C1 and C2

historic_results.role: foraging/predictive-carrier methodology pilot, NOT consciousness data
synchrony/perceptual-access confound studies, NOT consciousness data

literature_gate: C0 required; review ../literature/REVIEW_2026-10-31.md and BUTLIN_INDICATORS.json before claiming relevance
not_canonical_indicators_note: C1/C2/C3 are experimental assay families, not Butlin's 14 indicator IDs or a complete ontology of consciousness
